page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'INTRODUCTION', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The current government oversees the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (MDED), with the minister holds holding the status of a deputy prime minister, thus aknowledging the cross-cutting and interinstitutional nature of digital transformation-related issues.
interventions_named: Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation (minister with deputy prime minister status)
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'INTRODUCTION', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: On September 14th, 2023, the Government has approved the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, which includes, among its performance indicators, a clause that by the end of 2024 - 75% of all public services will be digitized, and by 2030 - all public services will be digital.
interventions_named: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030
intervention_as_stated: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to data provided by AGE, on the government portal of public services, there has been placed information on 714 available public services (out of which 283 or 39% are e-Services).
interventions_named: Government portal of public services
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This category of "e-Services" includes both fully automated electronic public services that allow for electronic self-service (services for which providers ensure the complete formalization and scheduling of the service delivery process) and partially automated electronic public services, which means services for which the physical interaction between service providers and beneficiaries is inevitable.
interventions_named: Government portal of public services
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Out of the 283 e-Services, 126 are related to the issuance of permissive documents and 157 are services for citizens and businesses.
interventions_named: Government portal of public services
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Out of the 157 public services that could be requested online, 36 (22.92%) are provided in digital format (services for which providers ensure the complete formalization and scheduling of the service delivery process).
interventions_named: Government portal of public services
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': 4, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: These include 12 cadastral services and 19 services for issuing civil status documents, apostilles, extracts from the state register of legal entities, proof of no debts to the state budget, personal social insurance account status, criminal records, detailed criminal records, and contravention records available in digital format, including the option for apostille and home delivery.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Recently, MDED has developed an interactive platform aimed at monitoring and informing the general public about public services for entrepreneurs in the Republic of Moldova. The platform indicates how many of these services are digitalized and their level of utilization.
interventions_named: MDED interactive platform monitoring public services for entrepreneurs
intervention_as_stated: MDED interactive platform on public services for entrepreneurs
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to MDED data, there are 523 public services in Moldova offered by 42 public institutions (ministries, agencies, inspectorates, specialized services, etc.), with 226 of them already digitalized, representing 43.2% of the total number.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In this context, we can highlight three distinct categories of institutions based on the number of digitized services within their competence area, with a noticeable variation in the approach to digitalization processes from one institution to another:
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 1. Institutions that have digitized all or most of the services provided (rate of 75% or more): National Road Transport Agency, National Agency for the Regulation of Nuclear and Radiological Activities, Environmental Protection Agency, National Bureau of Statistics, Land Relations and Cadastre Agency, and the Public Property Agency.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2. Institutions that have partially digitized their services (rate of 25-75%): Public Services Agency, Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices, Civil Aeronautics Authority, National Regulatory Authority for Electronic Communications and Information Technology, State Agency for Intellectual Property, State Fiscal Service, State Inspectorate of Public Security, Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (MDED), Information Technology Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, National Institute of Metrology, Chamber of Commerce and Industry, National Accreditation Center and National Health Insurance Company.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 3. Institutions that have digitized only a few public services (rate of 25% or less) or have not digitized any services: Naval Agency, National Agency for Food Safety, National Public Health Agency, National Technical Surveillance Inspectorate, National Radio Frequency Management Service, Customs Service, Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development, State Marking Supervision Authority.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: At the same time, several important public institutions have not digitized any services in their portfolio, including the Ministry of Education and Research, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, Geological and Mineral Resources Agency, Investment and Payments Agency for Agriculture, Transplant Agency, National Archives Agency, Agency for Energy Efficiency, National Agency for Quality Assurance in Education and Research, and the National Health Insurance House.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The development of digital solutions by responsible institutions is an ongoing process that requires continuous improvements, including the increase of penetration and usage by citizens.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The launch of a digital public service does not necessarily lead to its widespread use by beneficiaries.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 1. Digitized public services that are massively and predominantly used compared to the option offered at the institution's physical offices (50% or more of total service requests). These services are largely offered only in an online format or are easily accessible digital services with a very high penetration rate: authorization for the import of medicines, drug registration certificate (Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices), authorization for road transport of goods/INTERBUS carnet (National Road Transport Agency), partial radiological authorization (National Agency for the Regulation of Nuclear and Radiological Activities), waste management authorization (Environmental Protection Agency), statistical/financial reporting (National Bureau of Statistics), registration of taxable objects/standardized forms for special regime primary documents (State Fiscal Service), customs warehouse authorization (Customs Service), provision of topogeodetic materials (Land Relations and Cadastre Agency), initiation/termination of employment relationships (National Health Insurance Company), criminal record for individuals and legal entities (Information Technology Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs).
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2. Public services that are offered both in digital format and through requests at physical offices with a medium level of digital option usage (25-50%): coordination of dangerous goods transport route (National Road Transport Agency), certificate of property value/extract from the state register of legal entities (Public Services Agency), emission permit for pollutants/authorization for forestry clear-cutting (Environmental Protection Agency).
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 3. Digitized public services with low usage rates of 1-25%: non-scheduled flight authorization (Civil Aeronautics Authority), sanitary-veterinary authorization for means of transport (National Agency for Food Safety), operational sanitary permit for facilities (National Public Health Agency), non-preferential origin certificate for goods (Chamber of Commerce and Industry), nuclear/radiological security certificate (National Agency for the Regulation of Nuclear and Radiological Activities).
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 4. Digitized public services with negligible or non-existent usage rates (less than 1%): manufacturing authorization for medicines (Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices), individual permit for export/import of strategic goods, information about the property belonging to an individual/legal entity (Public Services Agency), authorization for the installation and operation of radio transmitters (Civil Aeronautics Authority), phytosanitary certificate for export/re-export (National Agency for Food Safety), environmental impact assessment/notification of cross -border waste transport (Environmental Protection Agency), presentation of aggregated data (National Bureau of Statistics), certificate of no arrears to the budget/tax code assignment/online registration of taxpayers (State Fiscal Service), provisional firearm permit/special category vehicle permit (State Inspectorate of Public Security), technical-professional qualification certificate for construction (Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development), detailed criminal record/contravention record (Information Technology Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs), all services of the National Institute of Metrology.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: A distinct category among these services consists of digital solutions reported to MDED as developed and functional but with zero users during the reporting period (2022). The total number of such services is 128, accounting for 56.63% of all reported digital services.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Therefore, according to the analysis, out of the 226 digital services reported to MDED, 77 services (34.07%), for which requests can be made both digitally and at the institutions' physical offices, had no digital requests in 2022 but had requests at the physical offices with a physical presence.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Additionally, another 51 digital public services (22.56%) have been reported by public institutions to MDED as having zero requests, both online and at the institutions' physical offices.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 1. The low number of users of qualified advanced electronic signatures, which represents the fundamental interface for accessing digital services.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to STISC data from September 2022, there were 129,384 active certificates of the public key for qualified advanced electronic signatures, of which 97,633 (75.45% of the total) were USB tokens: 18,400 were Mobile ID certificates issued by Orange Moldova, 17,725 were Mobile ID certificates issued by Moldcell, and 66 were eID cards issued by the Public Services Agency.
interventions_named: qualified advanced electronic signature certificates (STISC);Mobile ID;eID cards (Public Services Agency)
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: It should be noted that although 97,633 STISC certificates were issued, the number of unique users was much lower - 45,870, as many citizens possessed two (13,086), three (1,631) or more (345) certificates, even though holding multiple certificates is not necessary.
interventions_named: qualified advanced electronic signature certificates (STISC)
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2. Insufficient information provided to users and beneficiaries about the existence of developed digital solutions, their functionalities, advantages, and benefits.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Many functional digital services are poorly known to end users, with no clear and accessible communication channels for users to obtain additional information about their use or technical assistance, if needed.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 3. The complexity, lack of clarity, and non-intuitive interface of digital solutions.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': 7, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Additionally, some electronic public services might face performance issues, such as slow page loading, response delays, or frequent errors.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 4. People's resistance to change and preference for adherence to traditional methods.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 5. Negative previous experiences with the use of digital services.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 6. Limited access to technology and internet connectivity.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In rural areas, internet infrastructure might be underdeveloped or even nonexistent, making access to digital services practically impossible.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 7. Insufficient information security.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 8. Relatively low usage of online payments and e-commerce.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: It is essential for public service providers to be responsive to the suggestions of public service beneficiaries and continuously improve their electronic public services to meet the needs and expectations of citizens and the business environment.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 1. Increasing the number of users of digital signature certificates available in Moldova, including by organizing campaigns to inform users about the functionalities of digital signatures, the advantages they offer as access keys for all existing and prospective digital services.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Actions are needed to simplify the procedures for obtaining digital signatures and renewing the respective certificates.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2. Monetizing the use of digital signatures is a factor that hinders their widespread use.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Identifying possibilities to minimize the costs of obtaining and renewing digital signature certificates is necessary, as well as the use of digital signatures, including the removal of clauses limiting the number of digital signatures a citizen can apply.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 3. Developing digital signature certificates based on the MobiSign smartphone application, which is in the process of implementation and launch, can serve as a significant catalyst for the widespread use of digital services.
interventions_named: MobiSign smartphone signature application
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 3. Developing digital signature certificates based on the MobiSign smartphone application, which is in the process of implementation and launch, can serve as a significant catalyst for the widespread use of digital services.
interventions_named: MobiSign smartphone signature application
intervention_as_stated: MobiSign smartphone application
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The completion of audit procedures and the launch of MobiSign, accompanied by an extensive information campaign on how the solution works and how the security of processes and data is ensured, are necessary.
interventions_named: MobiSign smartphone signature application
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': 9, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 4. Developing digital solutions without considering the opinions of direct beneficiaries is a misguided perspective that directly affects the penetration and use of these solutions.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: By analogy, patients should be consulted in the case of digital solutions in the healthcare system, and students and parents should be consulted in the case of solutions in the field of education.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 5. Increasing the number of digital ambassadors who provide relevant information to any citizen is vital.
interventions_named: digital ambassadors
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: From this perspective, the establishment of 100 unique service delivery centers (CUPS) in rural regions of the Republic of Moldova by the end of 2023, in cooperation with local authorities, by the Agency for e-Government, is commendable.
interventions_named: Unified Public Service Centres (CUPS), 100 in rural areas (e-Governance Agency)
intervention_as_stated: 100 unique service delivery centres (CUPS) in rural regions
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: It is crucial for CUPS specialists to prioritize informing citizens about digital solutions and how they can be used.
interventions_named: Unified Public Service Centres (CUPS)
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In larger cities, specialists from the Multifunctional Centers of the Public Services Agency can play a fundamental role in this regard.
interventions_named: Multifunctional Centres of the Public Services Agency
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 6. Promoting digital leadership. Specialists from a ministry, agency, municipality, or regional council will not use digital solutions if the administration of these entities refuses or boycotts their use.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Clearer administrative protocols are necessary to limit the ability of decision-makers to halt or boycott the widespread implementation of digital solutions.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: At the same time, improving the digital skills of public sector employees and local authorities is necessary, including addressing the digital divide between urban and rural areas.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 7. Informing citizens about the security of their personal data used in the development of digital solutions, who accesses their data and why, and what limitations exist, is essential.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The objective of cybersecurity should be not only the direct responsibility of the specialized national institution (STISC), but also of basic cybersecurity programs within all state and educational institutions in the country.
interventions_named: Information Technology and Cyber Security Service (STISC)
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 9. Increasing nationwide internet coverage.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Despite having a solid internet connectivity network, internet accessibility remains a current issue, especially in rural regions, those far from major infrastructure and road networks, or those with lower incomes.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Increasing accessibility to fast internet access, developing free internet access points following the European Union's "WiFi4EU" model, and making connectivity devices accessible in public places (schools, libraries, municipalities) can minimize the exclusion of certain categories of citizens from the benefits of digital solutions.
interventions_named: WiFi4EU model of free internet access points
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'INTRODUCTION', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Republic of Moldova has placed the digitalization of public services among its development priorities.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: For individuals with limited financial resources, purchasing electronic devices or subscribing to internet services could be financially difficult.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Many functional digital services also require different procedures for making electronic payments. If these procedures are not coherent, the full provision of the digital service might not be possible.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAUSES OF THE REDUCED DEGREE OF USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Another related cause is the lack of trust or fear associated with making online payments, which could lead to reluctance or abandonment of the usage of a digital service.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 8, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING THE USE OF DIGITAL SERVICES IN MOLDOVA', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Ultimately, developers of digital solutions need to understand that these solutions are not intended only for narrowly specialized professionals. They are intended for all users and should, to the possible extent, be developed in a simple and intuitive manner.
institution: Institute for European Policies and Reforms (IPRE)

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Overview', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Internet access has increased, but penetration rates remain lower than other countries in the region.
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Overview', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Cyberattacks on both state entities and media outlets remain a significant issue.
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Overview', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The government recently adopted a cybersecurity legislative package to combat these problems.

intervention_as_stated: cybersecurity legislative package
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'I.1 Internet Access', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The reliability and speed of Moldova’s internet connections have generally improved.
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'I.1 Internet Access', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Moldova has fairly extensive internet coverage due to the country’s compact size and highly concentrated population.
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'I.1 Internet Access', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to 2022 data from the International Telecommunications Union, 63.5 percent of Moldovans use the internet, both on fixed or mobile networks.
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'I.1 Internet Access', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Moldova’s fixed internet service penetration rate was 33.5 percent for individuals, and 69.7 percent for households, on par with other European countries, per data from the National Regulatory Agency for Electronic Communications and Information Technology (ANRCETI).
institution: Freedom House

page: {'page': 425, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAPITOLUL 2 – LIBERA CIRCULAȚIE A LUCRĂTORILOR, INTRODUCERE', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to the 2025 European Commission Report, the Republic of Moldova has some level of preparation in the area of freedom of movement for workers.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 425, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAPITOLUL 2 – LIBERA CIRCULAȚIE A LUCRĂTORILOR, INTRODUCERE', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Considerable progress was made in signing bilateral agreements on the coordination of social security systems with EU Member States and in continuing preparatory work to join the European network of employment services (EURES) upon EU accession.

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 425, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CAPITOLUL 2 – LIBERA CIRCULAȚIE A LUCRĂTORILOR, INTRODUCERE', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}

page: {'page': 426, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1. Prezentarea generală a situației', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The legislation in force on labour migration treats citizens of the European Union as "foreign citizens", applying to them the same rules as to other categories of foreigners on the territory of the Republic of Moldova.
interventions_named: Labour migration legislation in force
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 426, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1. Prezentarea generală a situației', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: However, foreigners holding a temporary right of residence for work or study do not benefit from this access.
interventions_named: Law No. 105/2018 on employment promotion and unemployment insurance
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 426, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Currently, the provisions of Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners in the Republic of Moldova apply to EU citizens. Foreign citizens, including EU citizens, must obtain a temporary residence permit for work on the territory of the Republic of Moldova in order to be employed.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 426, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The above-mentioned law expressly provides that the temporary right of residence for work is granted for a period of up to one year, with the possibility of extension for a new term.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 427, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In 2023, amendments were made to Law No. 200/2010, under which citizens of EU Member States have the right, for 90 days in any period of 180 calendar days of stay on the territory of the Republic of Moldova, to work without obtaining a residence permit for work (without any formalities).
interventions_named: Amendments to Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners (2023)
intervention_as_stated: Amendments to Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners (2023)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 427, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence on the territory of the Republic of Moldova of citizens of the European Union and their family members, recently adopted, introduces a clear legal distinction between EU citizens and third-country nationals. This law significantly simplifies the documentation procedures applicable to EU citizens residing in the Republic of Moldova.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 privind libera circulație și șederea pe teritoriul Republicii Moldova a cetățenilor Uniunii Europene și a membrilor familiilor acestora
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 427, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: EU citizens will not be required to obtain a work authorisation or a residence permit for employment. For stays of up to 90 days, they may carry out lawful activities on the territory of the Republic of Moldova without additional formalities.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 (provisions applying on entry into force)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 427, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: For a stay exceeding 90 days, EU citizens will have to obtain a residence card, issued by the General Inspectorate for Migration (IGM), which is not conditional on a particular purpose of stay. The residence card is granted for up to 5 years and gives the holder the right to carry out any lawful activity, while guaranteeing the rights and obligations provided by national law.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members (residence card issued by the General Inspectorate for Migration)
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 (residence card for EU citizens)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The law (Law No. 105/2018) provides that foreign citizens with a temporary or permanent right of residence, recognised stateless persons and beneficiaries of international protection or political asylum (except foreigners with temporary residence for work or study) are subject to the same rules as Moldovan citizens in accessing, where needed, employment services and active measures.
interventions_named: Law No. 105/2018 on employment promotion and unemployment insurance
intervention_as_stated: Legea Nr. 105/2018 cu privire la promovarea ocupării forței de muncă și asigurarea de șomaj
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: EU citizens benefit from free access to all jobs in the Republic of Moldova, except public functions that expressly require Moldovan citizenship.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Under recent amendments made by Government Decision No. 566/2025 to Annex 5 to Government Decision No. 201/2009 on the application of the Law on the public function, posts in the categories "technical service post", "specialist post" and "auxiliary post" may be filled by persons without Moldovan citizenship or stateless persons, employed under an individual employment contract under the Labour Code.
interventions_named: Government Decision No. 566/2025 amending Annex 5 to Government Decision No. 201/2009 on the application of the Law on the public function
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 566/2025
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.1. Cadrul legislativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Following a detailed analysis of the legal acts on public service management, a decision will be taken on the category of functions or posts that may be opened to EU citizens.
interventions_named: Analysis of public service legislation to decide which functions or posts open to EU citizens
intervention_as_stated: Analysis of public service legislation to decide which posts open to EU citizens
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Within the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, about 35 persons are involved in transposing EU acts on access to the labour market, employment support, equality and social advantages.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The National Employment Agency (ANOFM) will play a central role in ensuring access of Member State citizens to employment services and active labour market measures.
interventions_named: National Employment Agency (ANOFM) role in access of Member State citizens to employment services and active measures
intervention_as_stated: Role of ANOFM in EU citizens' access to employment services
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In this context, the 35 territorial employment subdivisions will be involved, with a staff ceiling of 189 persons (including 9 posts under moratorium), of which 176 posts are filled.

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 428, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Labour Migration and EURES Directorate (staff ceiling 6 posts, of which 5 are filled);
interventions_named: Labour Migration and EURES Directorate of the National Employment Agency
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 429, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The National Social Insurance House employs 1084 specialists, of whom 732 in the territory and 352 in the central office.
interventions_named: National Social Insurance House (CNAS)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 429, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The State Labour Inspectorate (ISM) and its territorial subdivisions carried out 2599 inspections in 2024 on compliance with labour legislation, of which 1267 on employment relations, 46 on occupational safety and health, 1269 combined, and 17 on labour migration.
interventions_named: State Labour Inspectorate inspections (2024)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Under Article 5(8) of Law No. 200/2025, the Equality Council is given the competence to promote, monitor and support the application of the principle of equal treatment for EU citizens and their family members in exercising the right to free movement.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members, Art. 5(8): Equality Council
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025, art. 5(8): Equality Council as equal treatment body
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Equality Council will also act as national contact point for preventing and combating discrimination, responsible for cooperation with similar authorities in EU Member States and Schengen states, ensuring exchange of data and information with them for implementing this law.
interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members: Equality Council as national contact point
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025: Equality Council as national contact point
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Equality Council has 33 planned staff, of whom 19 are employed.
interventions_named: Equality Council
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Anti-discrimination Directorate (ceiling 7 posts, 4 filled), which assists Council members in examining and resolving complaints of alleged discrimination.
interventions_named: Equality Council Anti-discrimination Directorate
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: To ensure respect for the right to free movement, the Ministry of Internal Affairs is responsible for aligning policies on managing migration processes with European legislation.
interventions_named: Ministry of Internal Affairs
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 430, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Thus the Ministry of Internal Affairs together with the General Inspectorate for Migration are responsible for transposing Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of EU citizens and their family members to move and reside freely.
interventions_named: Ministry of Internal Affairs; General Inspectorate for Migration; Directive 2004/38/EC
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova (State Chancellery, Bureau for European Integration)

page: {'page': 431, 'page_end': None, 'section': '2.1.1.2. Cadrul administrativ', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In this context, in 2024 a cooperation agreement was signed between the General Inspectorate for Migration and the State Labour Inspectorate, regulating direct cooperation at central and territorial level on preventing and combating labour illegalities and on the regime of foreigners in Moldova.

intervention_as_stated: Acordul de colaborare IGM–ISM (2024)

interventions_named: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence of EU citizens and their family members; Regulation (EU) No 492/2011; Directive 77/486/EEC; Directive 2014/54/EU

interventions_named: Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030; Growth Plan for Moldova
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul I. INTRODUCERE', 'paragraph': '14', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 14. The Programme was drawn up through an inclusive and dynamic process, its content and actions being discussed and validated at meetings of the National Council for Digitalisation established by Order No. 165/2023 of the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation, and of the sector council on external assistance for the sectors coordinated by the Ministry, established by Order No. 60 of 20 May 2024, whose members are representatives of the institutions responsible for implementing the Programme's actions, academia and business associations in the sector.
interventions_named: National Council for Digitalisation (MEDD Order No. 165/2023)
intervention_as_stated: Consiliul Național pentru Digitalizare (Ordinul MDED nr. 165/2023)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '15', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 15. According to the digital transformation readiness assessment of Moldova carried out by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 2021, Moldova obtained 4.1 points out of 5, placing it at the differentiation stage, the fourth of five stages of readiness for digital transformation.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '17', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In 2024, 39.4% of citizens say they can use electronic services independently, 33.7% need occasional help and 24.8% prefer to delegate the obtaining of a service entirely.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '18', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In the first three quarters of 2024, 80.3% of requests for G2B services were made online and only 19.7% are still made at counters. G2C services, however, show moderate adoption: only 41% of total requests.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '19', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Young people aged 18 to 29 are the most active users of electronic services, using them three times more often than people aged 60-74.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '19', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: These discrepancies indicate an urgent need to reduce the digital divide and ensure access to electronic services for all categories of the population.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 5, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '19', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Interest in online public services peaked in 2024, with 47.4% of respondents using the internet to obtain information about medical services. In 2024, 40% of respondents said they had searched online for information about government organisations. There was also an increase in interest in information about cultural institutions (33.4%) and in requesting public services online (26.6%).
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '20', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2) Access to computers is higher in urban areas (67%) than in rural areas (41%), and this remains a major challenge that deepens the digital divide.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '20', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 4) There is a significant difference between high-income (72.4%) and low-income (23.4%) households in computer ownership. This indicator has fallen since 2022, when 40% of low-income households reported owning a computer, owing to the shift to various types of mobile devices.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '21', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 21. According to the Speedtest Global Index, which compares monthly internet access speed data for 100 countries, the Republic of Moldova ranks 57th for mobile broadband speed (download speed 50 Mbps, against a global average of 48 Mbps) and fortieth for fixed broadband speed (download speed 122 Mbps, above the global average of 98 Mbps).
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '22', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 22. Moldova is among the world leaders in the affordability of Gigabit internet for the population, over 90%, at affordable tariffs, which is an important advantage for developing the digital economy.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 6, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '22', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Combined with 98% 4G coverage and significant penetration of optical fibre, users have a wide range of options, but this degree of availability of high-speed networks does not yet have the expected economic and social impact.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '23', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 23. The total number of fixed broadband internet connections in the Republic of Moldova reached 825.2 thousand at the end of 2023, an increase of 4.6% on the third quarter of 2022 and of 25.9% on the third quarter of 2019, an increase of 169.5 thousand fixed internet subscribers.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '23', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: There was also a substantial increase in the number of mobile broadband internet customers, from 2.4 million in 2019 to 3.0 million at the end of 2023, an increase of 602.6 thousand.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '23', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Of a total of 1.1 million households, 825.2 thousand are connected to the internet, of which 747.5 thousand via optical fibre and 68.6 thousand via ADSL.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '24', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 24. Based on analysis of data from fixed internet providers, there are 431 localities in the Republic of Moldova that fall within the definition of 'white areas'.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '24', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Most of these localities are small and isolated, requiring significant investment to extend the broadband internet network.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '24', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In total, there are about 72 thousand households in white-area localities, or 6.3% of all households in the country.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '24', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: There is a direct correlation between the size of a locality and the chances that it lacks broadband internet.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '25', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Thus, 81.2% of respondents to the AGE survey said they access the internet via the mobile phone, up 3% on 2022 and 8% on 2021.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 7, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '26', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 26. Total traffic generated by mobile internet users in 2023 rose by about 25.9% or 67,341 TB on the previous year, of which smartphone users (voice users) generated traffic up about 35.6% or 71,891 TB, while dedicated mobile internet users consumed about 7.8% or 4,550 TB less, which clearly indicates users' device preferences
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '33', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 33. Health digitalisation is a growing priority for the Republic of Moldova, in the context of implementing the eRețeta system (over 270,000 reimbursed prescriptions issued monthly at the end of 2024) and of modernising digital platforms in the public medical sector. Currently, the SIA AMP information system is used by about 400 institutions and processes over 11 million consultations annually, including over 150,000 online appointments in 2024.
interventions_named: eRețeta e-prescription system; SIA AMP information system
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '33', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: However, the lack of a functional electronic health record, limited interoperability and the absence of a dedicated institutional framework remain major challenges.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '33', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Strategic Health Digitalisation Programme 2030, being drafted, provides for creating an integrated digital ecosystem coordinated by an entity dedicated to e-Health. It aims that, by 2030, over 50% of the insured population will have access to the Electronic Health Record, in line with the objectives of the Digital Transformation Strategy (STDM) and the standards of the European Health Data Space (EHDS).
interventions_named: Strategic Health Digitalisation Programme 2030 (being drafted)
intervention_as_stated: Programul strategic de digitalizare a sănătății 2030
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 34. The development of a digital society depends on the existence of an accessible digital identity widely adopted by citizens. In turn, the adoption of digital identity and electronic signature depends directly on the availability and use of electronic services that integrate these tools.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This condition was confirmed by the Information Technology and Cyber Security Service (STISC), which reported that demand for and use of the electronic signature service increased substantially when the Integrated Health Information System was implemented.
interventions_named: Integrated Health Information System
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: With only 10% of the population of the Republic of Moldova holding qualified certificates for electronic signature, genuine digital transformation remains a significant challenge.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This low adoption rate is all the more worrying since most current holders are public sector employees, obliged by the nature of their profession to use electronic signatures.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to data provided by STISC, on 30 September 2024 there were only 246,674 valid qualified certificates for electronic signature, including all types of electronic identification means (USB tokens, mobile IDs and electronic identity cards).
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 9, 'page_end': 10, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The situation is even more critical in the diaspora, where in 2023 only 67 electronic signature certificates were issued in the 41 diplomatic missions and consular offices, showing the extremely limited accessibility of currently existing digital services for Moldovan citizens abroad.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The low adoption of digital identity in the Republic of Moldova is the direct consequence of the limited accessibility of existing tools, combined with insufficient digitalisation of public services, which do not yet offer convincing benefits to justify the time and resources needed to obtain and use electronic identification means.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '34', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: To accelerate digital transformation and use available financial resources efficiently, the Government is to promptly prioritise the digitalisation and automation of public service delivery processes, as well as the implementation of a digital identity wallet.
interventions_named: Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '35', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 35. The electronic identity card, being launched by ASP, is an important step in this direction. It will include an embedded qualified digital certificate for creating electronic signatures, allowing citizens to sign documents online with full legal value.
interventions_named: Electronic identity card with qualified certificate (ASP)
intervention_as_stated: Cartea de identitate electronică
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '35', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In turn, institutions cooperate and reuse existing services; thus STISC together with ASP has extended the number of registration service providers so that qualified trust services are delivered through ASP offices throughout the country.
interventions_named: Delivery of qualified trust services through ASP offices
intervention_as_stated: Prestarea serviciilor de încredere calificate prin oficiile ASP
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '36', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 36. Also, the EVOSign service, launched in pilot mode on 8 August 2024, has shown remarkable potential for rapid adoption.
interventions_named: EVOSign service
intervention_as_stated: Serviciul EVOSign
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '36', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In just a few months after launch, the service attracted 15,450 users who completed registration and enabled 138,700 successful authentication sessions.
interventions_named: EVOSign service
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '36', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: For EVOSign to become a truly transformative solution, it must be extended and improved to function as a digital identity wallet in line with the rigorous standards of the European Union. This involves integrating qualified electronic signature functions and implementing remote identification and registration mechanisms for users. Alignment with the European digital wallet model (EUDI Wallet) would position the country in line with European digital trends and stimulate the adoption of digital identity without requiring considerable financial investment in services at risk of low use.
interventions_named: EVOSign service (as a digital identity wallet)
intervention_as_stated: Serviciul EVOSign
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 10, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '37', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 37. According to the survey carried out by the EU-funded Moldova cybersecurity rapid assistance project, although 61% of respondents are confident they have good or very good knowledge of online safety, there is a significant gap: only 19% know what phishing is and 27% understand the concept of cyberbullying.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 11, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '38', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 38. Despite efforts to strengthen cybersecurity, through creating the regulatory and institutional framework, primarily by creating the Cyber Security Agency, the number of cyberattacks in Moldova has increased significantly, by over 30% in the last three years.
interventions_named: Cyber Security Agency
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 11, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 1. Dezvoltarea Societății Digitale', 'paragraph': '38', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This alarming trend underlines the urgent need to intensify investment in cybersecurity and adopt more effective measures to protect critical infrastructure and citizens' personal data.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 13, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '45', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 45. The level of local market adoption of IT products and services developed by resident companies, in other sectors of the national economy, is relatively low compared with the sector's overall growth.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 13, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '46', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In recent years there has also been a significant increase in the number of foreign employees, a tenfold increase in 2023 compared with 2018.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 13, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '47', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 47. Although the first e-commerce regulations in Moldova date from 2004, the sector's development has been slow, lacking a coordinated effort by the authorities and consistent market demand.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 13, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '47', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Only in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic was more attention paid to e-commerce, and the authorities, together with the private sector and with USAID support, drew up a Roadmap to stimulate the sector's development, on the basis of which a series of substantial amendments to the relevant legislation were promoted.
interventions_named: Roadmap for the development of e-commerce (USAID support)
intervention_as_stated: Foaia de parcurs pentru dezvoltarea comerțului electronic
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '48', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 48. The eCommerce report for Moldova 'Recommendations for eCommerce harmonisation with the EU' of March 2024 records significant progress by the Republic of Moldova in improving its e-commerce ecosystem, applying digital marketing strategies similar to those of the EU, thus laying the foundations for successful integration into the largest online markets.
interventions_named: EU4Digital report Recommendations for eCommerce harmonisation with the EU (March 2024)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '48', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 2) Unjustified blocking or limiting of a customer's access to the trader's online interface, which is planned to be resolved by alignment with Regulation (EU) 2018/302 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 February 2018 on addressing unjustified geo-blocking and other forms of discrimination based on customers' nationality, place of residence or place of establishment within the internal market, amending Regulations (EC) No 2006/2004 and (EU) 2017/2394 and Directive 2009/22/EC.
interventions_named: Alignment with Regulation (EU) 2018/302 on geo-blocking (planned)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '50', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 50. At the end of 2023, 1,199 e-commerce platforms were registered, an increase of 57% compared with 2022.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '50', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: According to the National Bank of Moldova, the value of online payments on e-commerce platforms in 2023 was about EUR 500 million, of which EUR 365 million purchases on foreign platforms and EUR 135 million on local platforms.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '50', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Sales of tangible products and commercial services through e-commerce in Moldova, including cash on delivery, grew by 15.2% on the previous year, reaching an estimated EUR 358.6 million (excluding VAT) in 2023.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 14, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '50', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Overall, there is a visible digital divide in the market, with about 80% of the adult population excluded from e-commerce and the modern economy.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 15, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '54', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 54. E-commerce development is also constrained by SMEs' slow adoption of digital technologies. Lack of knowledge, high costs of implementing digital solutions and a return perceived as long term discourage many SMEs from improving their online presence.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 15, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '55', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 55. Currently, more than 60% of G2B public services are available electronically. About 2.5 out of 3 entrepreneurs prefer to use online services, and 5,392 entities use electronic invoicing.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 16, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '59', 'snapshot_file': None}

institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 16, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '60', 'snapshot_file': None}

page: {'page': 16, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '60', 'snapshot_file': None}
