page: {'page': 16, 'page_end': 17, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '61', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: In this regard, following the adoption of Law No. 48/2023 on cybersecurity, the Cyber Security Agency was established, which acts as the national cybersecurity incident response team (CERT) and national single point of contact, and will ensure the implementation of state policy, supervision and control in the field of cybersecurity.

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '62', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 62. The Network Readiness Index 2023 report places the Republic of Moldova 67th of 134 countries assessed on network readiness indicators.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '62', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Disaggregated data from this analysis show that our country performs best on population coverage by broadband networks, ranking 28th, network connection (FTTH/building internet subscriptions), 44th, device prices, 47th, internet service security, 48th, while the ICT regulatory framework is rated fairly easy, placing our country 34th.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '63', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 63. From another point of view, this international study identifies the weaknesses of the Republic of Moldova in readiness for the requirements of using the global network, namely: eCommerce legislation, 87th; investment in emerging technologies, 119th; global investment in electronic communications services, 108th; investment in R&D and universities, 86th; exports of products and services embedding advanced technologies (except ICT), 94th; digital payments in rural regions, 93rd; software spending, 93rd; privacy protection, 109th.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '64', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 64. The Republic of Moldova has evolved enormously in implementing advanced models of electronic communications market regulation, which has contributed greatly to the sector's development, according to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), but new measures are needed to adjust the institutional framework for policy development and market regulation mechanisms.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '64', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The ITU finds insufficient independence and accountability of the regulatory authority, and digital economy development policies must emphasise digital competitiveness, which can be significantly improved by using collaborative regulation tools, pro-competitive reforms in all areas related to digital transformation, regulatory incentives for innovation, and solid, enforceable mechanisms for consumer protection in the digital age.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '64', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The ITU finds insufficient independence and accountability of the regulatory authority, and digital economy development policies must emphasise digital competitiveness, which can be significantly improved by using collaborative regulation tools, pro-competitive reforms in all areas related to digital transformation, regulatory incentives for innovation, and solid, enforceable mechanisms for consumer protection in the digital age.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '64', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Another important aspect concerns the lack of a single framework for managing and monitoring the implementation of digital economy and ICT sector development policies.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 17, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '65', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 65. On 23 August 2024, ANRCETI approved the Standard Licence Conditions, under which holders of licences to use frequencies in the 700 MHz and 800 MHz bands are obliged to provide cumulative coverage with mobile broadband communications services, with 4G and 5G radio signal, of at least 75% by 31 October 2027 with an average downlink data rate to the user, in indoor reception conditions, of at least 30 Mbps, and by 31 October 2035 of at least 60 Mbps.
interventions_named: ANRCETI Standard Licence Conditions (700 MHz and 800 MHz)
intervention_as_stated: Condițiile tip de licență (ANRCETI)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 18, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '66', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 66. On 4 October 2024, ANRCETI announced the launch of the competition for issuing licences to use radio frequencies in the 700 MHz, e900 MHz, 1500 MHz, 2300 MHz, 2600 MHz, 3600 MHz and 26 GHz bands to provide public mobile/fixed terrestrial radio electronic communications networks and publicly available mobile/fixed electronic communications services.
interventions_named: ANRCETI competition for radio frequency licences (October 2024)
intervention_as_stated: Concursul pentru eliberarea licențelor de utilizare a frecvențelor radio
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 18, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 2. Dezvoltarea Sectorului TIC și a Economiei Digitale', 'paragraph': '67', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 67. The results of the competition and the fees due for licences to use radio frequencies in the 700 MHz, e900 MHz, 1500 MHz, 2300 MHz, 2600 MHz, 3600 MHz and 26 GHz bands were announced on 30 January 2025. Following the competition procedures, three bidders were awarded radio frequencies in the 700 MHz, 1500 MHz, 3400-3800 MHz and e900 MHz bands.
interventions_named: ANRCETI competition for radio frequency licences
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '68', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 68. In recent years, the Republic of Moldova has made progress in developing and modernising the common e-Government infrastructure.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '68', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Multiple reusable digital platforms have been successfully developed and implemented, such as MCloud, MPass, MPay, MConnect, MNotify, MPower, MSign, MTender, MDelivery, MCabinet, MLearn, particip.gov.md and raportare.gov.md.
interventions_named: MCloud; MPass; MPay; MConnect; MNotify; MPower; MSign; MTender; MDelivery; MCabinet; MLearn; particip.gov.md; raportare.gov.md
intervention_as_stated: Platformele digitale reutilizabile de e-Guvernare (MCloud, MPass, MPay, MConnect, MNotify, MPower, MSign, MTender, MDelivery, MCabinet, MLearn)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '68', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: These tools have played an essential role in transforming the public sector, facilitating quick and efficient access to electronic services provided by the public sector.
interventions_named: Reusable e-government platforms
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '69', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 69. The public services portal, which records over 0.5 million unique visitors annually, works as a one-stop shop for all public services. It provides direct access to 303 electronic services, as well as detailed information on 350 other public services and life events, for both citizens and companies.
interventions_named: Public services portal
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '70', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 70. Adoption of the MCabinet portal is growing exponentially, as shown by the doubling of the number of unique authenticated users, from 92,619 in the whole of 2023 to 176,855 in only the first three quarters of 2024.
interventions_named: MCabinet portal
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '71', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 71. Another important step in improving citizen-state interaction was the launch in June 2024 of the government mobile application for integrated public services, EVO. The EVO application brings government services, documents, data and payments within reach of every citizen through mobile devices.
interventions_named: EVO government mobile application
intervention_as_stated: Aplicația mobilă guvernamentală EVO
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '71', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: By 23 December 2024 the application had recorded a total of 72,400 downloads and 70,000 documents generated in citizens' electronic wallet.
interventions_named: EVO government mobile application
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '71', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The application is also actively used for electronic payments: by 23 December 2024, 2,700 payments totalling MDL 1,608,000 had been processed through EVO.
interventions_named: EVO government mobile application
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '72', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 72. Moldova ranked 70th in the UN E-Government Development Index in 2024, below Estonia (2), Lithuania (21) and Latvia (29). Although it overtook Romania (72) and Belarus (77), there is a significant gap with the regional leaders.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '73', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 73. In 2022 Moldova was ranked in group A of the most advanced countries in the GovTech Maturity Index, demonstrating robust digital infrastructure and efficient implementation of e-government solutions.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '74', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 74. However, major challenges remain regarding user-centricity, transparency in service design and delivery, and cross-border services.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '74', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This is highlighted in the E-Government Benchmark 2024 report, in which Moldova was included for the first time in 2024 but ranked last in Europe, with a score of 32 out of 100.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '75', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 75. In 2024, through developing the e-APL platform and extending the network of unified public service delivery centres (CUPS), a significant step was taken towards more efficient and accessible public administration at local level, facilitating citizens' access to digital public services and improving their communication with central and local public authorities and institutions.
interventions_named: e-APL platform; Unified Public Service Delivery Centres (CUPS)
intervention_as_stated: Platforma e-APL; Centrele unificate de prestare a serviciilor publice (CUPS)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 19, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '75', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Thus, about 100 electronic public services are currently provided in the 103 CUPS.
interventions_named: Unified Public Service Delivery Centres (CUPS)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '76', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 76. Since 2011, Moldova has launched the open government data initiative, publishing over 1,268 datasets on the date.gov.md portal.
interventions_named: Open government data initiative (date.gov.md)
intervention_as_stated: Inițiativa de deschidere a datelor guvernamentale (date.gov.md)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '76', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Today the platform needs updating and completing with data, to remove barriers to access to and reuse of public data. It is also imperative to align the national regulatory framework with the European one in this field.
interventions_named: date.gov.md open data portal
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '77', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 77. According to recent AGE data, 144 state information systems and 252 private information systems are integrated in MConnect, 633 data exchange scenarios are implemented and there are about 1.5 million successful queries per day.
interventions_named: MConnect interoperability platform
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '77', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: However, despite a favourable legal framework and technological tools, government information systems remain fragmented, and in many cases replacing documents with the provision of data remains problematic.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '77', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This situation is aggravated by the lack of complete digitalisation of some essential registers, such as those on immovable property or civil status records, which leads to redundant processes and inefficient data exchange between institutions.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '79', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 79. The MCloud platform faces limits in its capacity to meet the growing demand for resources and services of central and local public administration.
interventions_named: MCloud
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '79', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: To address this challenge, an approach based on developing a hybrid cloud infrastructure is to be applied, combining existing MCloud resources with public cloud services, thus optimising costs and compensating for the shortage of human and financial resources. This transformation will allow public institutions to benefit from modern cloud computing technologies, while ensuring compliance with security and data protection requirements.
interventions_named: Hybrid cloud infrastructure (MCloud and public cloud)
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '80', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 80. One of the main problems is the existence of outdated and fragmented information systems that do not allow effective interoperability between government institutions.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '80', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Although there is a solid regulatory framework, including Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability and Government Decision No. 211/2019 on the interoperability platform (MConnect), and advanced electronic tools covering all levels of interoperability (technical, semantic, organisational and legal) have been implemented, in many cases replacing documents with the provision of data remains problematic.
interventions_named: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability; Government Decision No. 211/2019 on the MConnect interoperability platform
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 142/2018 privind schimbul de date și interoperabilitate; Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 211/2019 privind platforma de interoperabilitate (MConnect)
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '81', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 81. The lack of common product development and design standards for government platforms leads to a fragmented and inconsistent experience for users, who face different and hard-to-navigate interfaces on each platform.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 20, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '82', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 82. Public authorities often adopt digital technologies without redesigning traditional processes to suit the online environment, thus replicating existing inefficiencies and bureaucracy.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 21, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '83', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 83. Consequently, the digital transformation of public administration is hampered by multiple challenges, from fragmented technological infrastructure and lack of interoperability of systems, to a shortage of qualified staff and resistance to change at institutional level.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 21, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '83', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: However, the most important barrier is the lack of centralised coordination of digitalisation initiatives at Government level, and the lack of adequate mechanisms at MDED level to implement the regulatory framework, investments and projects in the field.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 21, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '84', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 84. Experience so far has highlighted the need for standardisation, modernisation and reuse of IT infrastructure and for developing digital skills in the public sector. An important lesson is the need for a citizen-centred approach that prioritises simplifying interfaces and processes for users. Also, alignment with EU regulations and integration into the European digital single market are essential steps for the success of Moldova's digital transformation.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 21, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '85', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 85. The importance of a solid framework for interoperability and centralisation of data is also highlighted, with a focus on improving data quality, availability and correct classification. Experience has shown that fragmentation of state registers, lack of full interoperability and the absence of clear data classification have led to inconsistent information, inefficient management of sensitive data and difficulties in ensuring appropriate access to data.
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 21, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul II. ANALIZA SITUAȚIEI CURENTE, Secțiunea 3. e-Transformarea sectorului public', 'paragraph': '85', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: To overcome these challenges, it is essential to implement a governance framework and common standards for collecting, storing, classifying and sharing data between institutions, and to develop robust mechanisms for validating, securing and continuously updating information according to its sensitivity and strategic importance.
interventions_named: Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030
institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova; Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization

page: {'page': 22, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Capitolul III. OBIECTIVE GENERALE', 'paragraph': '88', 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 88. To achieve the vision, six General Objectives are identified, namely: 1) developing a digital society; 2) developing a robust and competitive ICT sector; 3) creating an innovative and resilient digital economy; 4) establishing an efficient, smart and transparent digital state; 5) creating an accessible, secure and inclusive digital environment; 6) consolidating the image of the Republic of Moldova as a digital nation.
interventions_named: Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030

page: {'page': 90, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CHAPTER III ACTIVITY OF REPRESENTATION IN THE COURTS', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The parallel examination, in different procedures – administrative litigation and contravention – of the same findings by the NCPDP continues to represent a structural issue affecting legal predictability and the operational efficiency of the authority. page: {'page': 90, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'CHAPTER III ACTIVITY OF REPRESENTATION IN THE COURTS', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Furthermore, the analysis of case law highlights the persistence of divergent solutions by the courts: in some cases, the findings of the NCPDP are upheld in administrative litigation but overturned in contravention proceedings, or vice versa. text: This situation is expected to change with the entry into force of Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, which introduces a new mechanism for applying sanctions, namely, the administrative sanction. page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening summary (untitled)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Over 130,000 Ukrainian refugees in Moldova, primarily skilled women, represent an untapped economic asset.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening summary (untitled)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Despite documented labour shortages, only 29 percent of working-age refugees are in paid work.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening summary (untitled)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Survey findings point to systemic barriers: language gaps (36 percent of job seekers), skills mismatch and non-recognition of diplomas (13 percent), and scarce, affordable childcare.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening summary (untitled)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: While Temporary Protection (TP) grants the right to work, these obstacles drive underemployment and reliance on social assistance.
interventions_named: Temporary protection (right to work)
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening summary (untitled)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Recommended measures include sector-specific Romanian language programmes, fast-track credential recognition, expansion of subsidized childcare, micro-grants for entrepreneurship, and employer-focused job-matching through the Agenția Națională pentru Ocuparea Forței de Muncă (ANOFM)—Moldovan National Employment Agency.
interventions_named: Agenția Națională pentru Ocuparea Forței de Muncă (ANOFM) job-matching
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Context and Opportunity', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Refugees seeking employment often encounter Romanian-language requirements, unclear regulations, informal hiring practices, scarce childcare, and limited access to credit, training, and information.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Context and Opportunity', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Testimonies reveal a large share of people who are unemployed, in precarious jobs, and experiencing rising psychological stress, even though labour shortages persist in agriculture, hospitality, social care, construction, and IT.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Context and Opportunity', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Temporary protection status formally grants unrestricted access to work, yet in practice, many refugees accept low-skilled positions because vacancies in their own professions are rare, and employers often require different skill sets.
interventions_named: Temporary protection (access to work)
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Context and Opportunity', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Fragmented, underfunded support services further blunt integration efforts.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Human Capital', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The potential is substantial as more than 80 percent of working-age refugee respondents (18–64 years) report having professional experience, 77 percent hold vocational or higher qualifications, and 63 percent are keen to join self-employment programmes.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Human Capital', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Only 29 percent, however, have found paid work, over half of households rely mainly on social assistance, and nearly half of job seekers cite insufficient Romanian language as their primary barrier to employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Human Capital', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Targeted language courses, affordable childcare, streamlined recognition of qualifications, and coordinated funding could unlock the potential of this workforce and benefit Moldova’s economy.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Obstacles to Economic Participation – Language Barriers', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Limited Romanian language skills are the most frequently cited obstacle for adult refugees. Approximately 36 percent of refugees report this as a significant barrier to employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Obstacles to Economic Participation – Mismatch of Skills and Jobs', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Around 13 percent of refugees cannot find job openings relevant to their professional background or education level. This leads to underemployment or engaging in time-bound/seasonal employment, as many highly skilled individuals are offered low-skilled jobs or jobs outside their expertise.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Obstacles to Economic Participation – Mismatch of Skills and Jobs', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Barriers to the recognition of foreign credentials also persist.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Obstacles to Economic Participation – Limited Childcare Options', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: A lack of affordable childcare is a major constraint, especially since most refugees are women and often sole caregivers. While this issue is common for both refugees and host community members, 11 percent of refugee households cited limited access to childcare as a barrier to employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 2, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Obstacles to Economic Participation – Lower Wages & Limited Access to Credit', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Around 10 percent of refugees perceive that salaries in Moldova are too low compared to what they earned in Ukraine. The income gap, combined with rising inflation and living costs, can discourage skilled refugees from accepting offers of employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Information Gaps & Limited Uptake of ANOFM', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Around 2 percent of refugees lack information on how and where to look for jobs in Moldova. For 39 percent, support with identification and job matching is the most preferred form of assistance to secure employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Information Gaps & Limited Uptake of ANOFM', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Formal employment services, like ANOFM, remain underutilized.
interventions_named: ANOFM employment services
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Employer Reluctance', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: While the legal framework is not the primary barrier, administrative challenges can still slow down labour market integration.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Employer Reluctance', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Some employers are reluctant to hire refugees due to assumed legal complexities or limited awareness of candidates’ skills and qualifications.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Employer Reluctance', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Although language proficiency is the most frequently cited individual barrier, a broader analysis suggests that structural weaknesses in Moldova’s labour market—such as skills mismatches, low wages, and limited job availability—represent the main constraints to employment. Taken together, these systemic factors outweigh specific integration challenges such as language or childcare needs.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Employer Reluctance', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: This indicates that many of the key impediments are structural and affect both refugees and the host population, pointing to the need for longer-term labour market and economic reforms rather than short-term programmatic interventions.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Key Prospects and Opportunities – Strong Skills and Experience', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: 76 percent of adult refugees have at least vocational or tertiary education, and 81 percent report having previous professional work experience. However, only 34 percent have engaged in paid work since arriving in Moldova.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Key Prospects and Opportunities – Willingness to Work and Adapt', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Refugees demonstrate strong motivation to become self-reliant, with 22 percent actively looking for work in the four weeks before the survey. Notably, 63 percent expressed interest in a self-employment support programme.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Key Prospects and Opportunities – Partial Employment Gains', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Despite the challenges, around 29 percent of refugees have engaged in paid work since arriving in Moldova.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Key Prospects and Opportunities – Supportive Social Networks', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Most employed refugees (around 61 percent) found jobs through friends or acquaintances, highlighting the role of informal networks and community connections in facilitating employment.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Recommendations – Human Capital', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Expand employment-focused Romanian language courses.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Recommendations – Human Capital', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Implement fast-track diploma recognition programmes and organize refugee employment fairs, complemented by increased outreach and strengthened assistance through ANOFM.
interventions_named: Fast-track diploma recognition programmes; refugee employment fairs; ANOFM assistance
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Recommendations – Care and Finance', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Simplify procedures for registering self-employment and/or establishing an individual legal entity and provide micro-grants alongside mentorship to support refugee entrepreneurship.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 4, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Recommendations – Information and Administrative', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Continue providing legal work permits and actively promote employment opportunities to both refugees and local businesses.
interventions_named: Legal work permits for refugees
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': '(opening summary, no heading)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: Implemented through clear lead agencies and partner coordination, these measures can accelerate inclusion and reduce fiscal pressure.
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 3, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Key Prospects and Opportunities', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': None}
text: The Ukrainian refugee population in Moldova presents a significant talent pool that could be leveraged better in the labour market
institution: UNHCR

page: {'page': 1, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Opening paragraphs (no heading)', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Efforts by Moldova’s government and international actors have begun to build the country’s cyber capacity. Nonetheless, several factors mean Moldova remains vulnerable to cyber operations.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: It has low government revenue compared with its European peers and several pressing priorities for state expenditure. Socio-economic challenges including a contracting population, an over-reliance on remittances and inflation detract from the government’s ability to spend on cyber security.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: As demonstrated by the large-scale cyber incidents suffered by Albania and Costa Rica , small states which are unable or choose not to spend on cyber security are highly vulnerable to significant impact.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: While accusations have primarily been levelled within the political sphere , infiltration also impacts national cyber security. An insider could, for instance, grant hostile actors access to critical systems.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: From mid-2022 to early 2023, a series of high-profile attacks have targeted government credibility. ‘Hack-and-leak’ operations have compromised, exfiltrated and published confidential documents , while DDoS attacks and exposures from spear phishing campaigns have disrupted state services.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Despite challenges, Moldova is committed to and proactive in developing its cyber security capacity.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: For example, the country has steadily adopted regulatory best practices, such as legislating for critical infrastructure providers to adopt prescribed cyber security measures.
interventions_named: Legislation requiring critical infrastructure providers to adopt prescribed cyber security measures
intervention_as_stated: Legislation requiring critical infrastructure providers to adopt prescribed cyber security measures
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Moldova has furthermore broadly sought to digitalise in a cyber-secure manner. E-government services have expanded significantly and are notable for adopting cloud-based solutions such as MCloud, MPay and MSign .
interventions_named: MCloud; MPay; MSign
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: In April 2023, for example, the government changed MCloud operating regulations to allow for cloud hybridisation. This permitted the use of foreign public cloud services , provided by data centres in EU member states, and responded to emerging best practices established by Ukraine’s cyber defence using distributed cloud servers.
interventions_named: Amendment of the MCloud operating regulations (April 2023) allowing cloud hybridisation
intervention_as_stated: Amendment of MCloud operating regulations to allow cloud hybridisation
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: These amendments illustrate that Moldova has a strategic awareness of the emerging importance of interoperable cloud technologies in the context of national cyber security and systems integrity.
interventions_named: Amendment of the MCloud operating regulations (April 2023)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Nonetheless, Moldova’s cyber security ecosystem remains ‘ fragmented ’.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: The country suffers from the global gap in qualified cyber professionals and therefore struggles to implement cyber security improvements.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: For example, in November 2022, the Government Cyber Emergency Response Team (CERT-GOV-MD) had a staff of four .
interventions_named: Government Cyber Emergency Response Team (CERT-GOV-MD)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Moldova’s wider institutional gaps are reflected in its Global Cybersecurity Index ranking, which fell from 53rd to 63rd between 2018 and 2020.
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Attributes of Vulnerability', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: This indicates that, relative to its peers, Moldova still needs to drive improvements including establishing a cyber threats analysis unit, bringing forward the implementation of its new cyber security law , and participating in more international exercises.
interventions_named: New cyber security law (not named in the item)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: For example, the Estonian eGovernance Academy has supported legislative, strategic and organisational reforms over the past decade .
interventions_named: Estonian eGovernance Academy cyber capacity building support
intervention_as_stated: Estonian eGovernance Academy cyber capacity building support
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: From early 2022, Czechia and Romania have also commenced bi-lateral cyber-assistance programmes with Moldova, aiming to enhance cyber resilience through information-sharing, strengthening government capacities to engage on cyber security policy, and encouraging cross-border public-private partnerships.
interventions_named: Bilateral cyber-assistance programmes of Czechia and Romania
intervention_as_stated: Bilateral cyber-assistance programmes of Czechia and Romania with Moldova
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: In May 2022, the EU launched the Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme to improve cyber resilience across the public sector and key critical infrastructure sectors.
interventions_named: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme (EU)
intervention_as_stated: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: The project aims to develop diverse capacity outcomes including adjusting the 'normative-legislative framework of cybersecurity’, increasing societal awareness and hygiene, and developing targeted technical skills.
interventions_named: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme (EU)
intervention_as_stated: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme (aims)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: It does not, however, provide or commit to operational support for Moldova’s cyber defence.
interventions_named: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme (EU)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: In April 2023, participating EU member states announced the deployment of a Cyber Rapid Response Team (CRRT) to Moldova to aid the government in securing its national cyberspace. The CRRT forms part of the EU’s Permanent Structured Cooperation Framework.
interventions_named: Cyber Rapid Response Team (CRRT) deployment (PESCO)
intervention_as_stated: Cyber Rapid Response Team (CRRT) deployment to Moldova
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Existing Efforts', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Furthermore, in December 2022, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development partnered with private-sector cyber security providers to enhance cyber resilience for SMEs in Moldova , given that these types of organisations have been severely impacted by cyber attacks.
interventions_named: EBRD partnership with private-sector cyber security providers for SME cyber resilience
intervention_as_stated: EBRD partnership with private-sector cyber security providers for SME cyber resilience
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Filling the Gaps', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: First, CERT-GOV-MD and an external technical body that will take responsibility for coordinating future international assistance should prepare and maintain a list of Moldova’s immediate operational needs should a national cyber incident occur. This would cover activities to rapidly improve cyber defences, such as deploying private-sector incident responders.
interventions_named: Government Cyber Emergency Response Team (CERT-GOV-MD)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Filling the Gaps', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Second, ‘hunt forward’-style operations – pioneered by US Cyber Command – should be undertaken on Moldova’s networks. These will commission leading cyber security companies to identify existing vulnerabilities and any attackers that have compromised Moldovan networks. This should also then feed back into longer-term CCB activities, such as the EU’s Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme, to inform the improvement of Moldova’s underlying capacity.
interventions_named: Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance programme (EU)
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Filling the Gaps', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
text: Finally, Moldova should be fast-tracked for involvement in NATO’s Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE) exercises.
interventions_named: NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE) exercises
institution: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI)

page: {'page': None, 'page_end': None, 'section': 'Filling the Gaps', 'paragraph': None, 'snapshot_file': 'sources/MDA/RES/originals/MDA-RES-2023-001_RUSI-Battening-Down-the-Hatches-Moldova-Cyber-Defence.html'}
